name: Jasmine Jasudavicius
event: UFC Fight Night: Buckley vs. Malott
summary: The No. 6-7 flyweight (15-4, 9-3 UFC), a big, physical Niagara Top Team grinder whose game is takedowns, heavy top control and late submissions. Bounced back from her first career stoppage loss (Manon Fiorot, TKO R1, October 2025) with a grinding decision over Karine Silva, and fights at home with the delay from August having reshaped her camp.

how_they_fight.Striking: Functional but limited: about 3.4 significant strikes a minute and about 54% striking defense. Her striking exists to close distance and clinch. Fiorot hit her clean with a right hand and finished her in 74 seconds while she landed 2 of 14.
how_they_fight.Grappling: The engine. Wrestles from the clinch, holds top position and wears opponents down with ground-and-pound: 489 seconds of control on Karine Silva (3 of 5 takedowns), 431 on Mayra Bueno Silva, 685 on Priscila Cachoeira. Per LowKick MMA she now has the second-most control time in UFC women's flyweight history. Survived Silva's triangle and guard attacks without trouble.
how_they_fight.Defense: Stopped once in 19 pro fights (Fiorot). Takedown defense around 68%. Losses to Natalia Silva (0-for-6 on takedowns) and Tracy Cortez (2-for-10) came when her wrestling was stuffed and she had to strike.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Slow burner: nine of 15 wins are decisions, and two of her three UFC submissions came in round three (Cachoeira 4:21, Ariane Lipski da Silva 2:28); only Jessica Andrade went early (R1). Pace and pressure grow as rounds go on. Her only stoppage loss came early (R1).
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Disciplined, knows her path: clinch, takedown, control, repeat. Has rarely shown a plan B when the takedowns don't land.

patterns: Clinch against the fence -> takedown -> long top control with ground-and-pound
Late finisher: UFC subs in R3 (2) and R1 (1); otherwise decisions (9 of 15 career wins)
Wins rounds with control time rather than damage
Struggles when she can't get the fight down (Natalia Silva, Cortez)
Only stoppage loss: early, on the feet, to a sharp striker (Fiorot R1)

Uses her size in the grappling: out-wrestled and back-took Blanchfield, a better-credentialed grappler, for two rounds; the owner's note: "Jasmine uses her size really well in grappling" (owner's notes, UFC Fight Night: Buckley vs. Malott)
concerns: Chin/defence on the feet after the Fiorot knockout
Facing a better pure grappler than herself: Blanchfield's back takes punish wrestling exchanges
Said the two-month delay from Blanchfield's injury affected her camp (BJPenn.com podcast)
keys_to_beat: Stuff the clinch and early takedowns; make her strike
Land clean straight punches as she closes distance
Scramble and threaten from the bottom; don't let her settle
Bank the early rounds before her grind takes over

news.text: Her August 15 UFC 330 fight with Blanchfield was moved to UFC Edmonton after Blanchfield's injury, giving her a home fight in the co-main.
Discussed on Just Scrap Radio how the injury delay on Blanchfield's side affected her training camp.
Underdog at +240 against Blanchfield (-300), per MMA Junkie.

Media day: said she had a full camp done for August ('my weight was good') and used the delay to rest; expects Blanchfield to shoot more 'once she feels these hands' and calls the bout a title eliminator.
Official weigh-in: 124.5 lb for the women's flyweight bout; no misses reported on the card.
Beat Erin Blanchfield by unanimous decision (29-28 x3 on Sherdog): two takedowns and a back take with a body triangle in R1, the same in R2, lost R3 on the feet.
